n: This begins a final group of psalms credited to David (138–145). He praises God wholeheartedly — even ‘before the gods,’ boldly honoring the Lord in the face of any rival powers or rulers.

f.g: Possibly heavenly beings, the gods of the nations, or human rulers.

n: He bows toward the temple and praises God’s covenant love and faithfulness. God has honored his word — his promise — even above his own reputation.

f.w: magnified thy word above all thy name
f.g: Exalted your promise above everything else known of you.

n: When he cried out, God answered and made him bold, putting strength into his soul.

f.w: strengthenedst me with strength in my soul

n: All earth’s kings will praise the Lord when they hear his words.

f.w: All the kings of the earth

n: They will sing of the Lord’s ways, for his glory is great.

f.w: great is the glory of the LORD

n: Though the Lord is exalted, he cares for the humble; but he keeps his distance from the proud, seeing them from afar.
Even in the middle of trouble, God will preserve his life, stretching out his hand against enemies and saving him with his right hand.

f.w: Though I walk in the midst of trouble

n: The Lord will finish what he has begun in David’s life. His love lasts forever, so David asks him not to abandon the work of his own hands.

f.w: The LORD will perfect that which concerneth me
the works of thine own hands
